title: CrowdStrike to Buy Jay Chaudhry's Zscaler in $43.9 Billion All-Stock Deal
excerpt: The definitive agreement pays Zscaler shareholders 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, an implied $260.41, with Chaudhry staying on to run Zscaler and join the CrowdStrike board.
body:
• CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler, founded and led by Indian American chief executive Jay Chaudhry, in an all-stock deal valuing Zscaler at approximately $43.9 billion.
  • Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share — an implied $260.41 per share based on CrowdStrike's November 20 close, a premium of approximately 34%.
  • After closing, existing CrowdStrike shareholders are expected to own approximately 84.1% of the combined company and Zscaler shareholders approximately 15.9%.
  • Chaudhry, whose affiliates hold approximately 34% of Zscaler's shares and have backed the deal, will continue to lead the Zscaler business and join CrowdStrike's board. Closing is expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028, between August 1, 2027 and January 31, 2028.

CrowdStrike will acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction that values Zscaler at approximately $43.9 billion, the two companies announced on Monday, November 23. Zscaler was founded by Jay Chaudhry, who serves as its chief executive and chairman and will continue to lead the business after the deal closes.

Under the definitive agreement announced by the companies, each outstanding share of Zscaler common stock will be exchanged for 1.135 shares of CrowdStrike common stock. Based on CrowdStrike's closing share price on November 20, 2026, that represents an implied value of approximately $260.41 per Zscaler share — a premium of approximately 34% to Zscaler's closing price that day. The agreement was unanimously approved by both boards.

"We built Zscaler to bring a new approach to the cybersecurity industry and that is a Zero Trust architecture. In the AI era, Zero Trust security has become non-negotiable, and AI agents are rapidly becoming the new weakest link."

— Jay Chaudhry, CEO, chairman and founder of Zscaler, in the joint announcement

What was reported

The transaction is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028, subject to approval by Zscaler shareholders, receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. That period runs from August 1, 2027 to January 31, 2028, CRN reported. Until closing, both companies will continue to operate independently.

Chaudhry and his affiliates, representing approximately 34% of Zscaler's outstanding shares, have entered into voting agreements in support of the transaction, the companies said. Following the close, Chaudhry will join the CrowdStrike board of directors while continuing to run Zscaler.

Why the companies say they are combining

CrowdStrike is a leader in securing endpoints, workloads, identity and data; Zscaler secures the connections between them through its Zero Trust Exchange. With Zscaler, CrowdStrike said it will enter network security, which it called cybersecurity's largest single addressable market segment, and offer Zscaler's Zero Trust SASE, security for AI and data protection as part of its Falcon platform.

"With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike chief executive George Kurtz said in the announcement. Chaudhry called the two companies complementary and the agreement "the natural evolution of our longstanding partnership."

CRN reported the planned acquisition is positioned to become the largest acquisition of a pure-play cybersecurity vendor to date, topping Google's $32 billion acquisition of Wiz, which closed in March.

The figures the companies published

At closing, the combined company is expected to begin with more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue. Zscaler reported $3.9 billion of ARR as of its recently completed fiscal quarter, protects 50 percent of the Fortune 500, and operates its inline security cloud across more than 200 service locations, according to the announcement. Approximately 8,000 Zscaler customers are not yet CrowdStrike customers, and CrowdStrike estimates the acquisition will expand its total addressable market by more than $185 billion in calendar year 2029.

The companies' synergy figures are expectations, not results: CrowdStrike expects revenue synergies to reach approximately $1 billion in annualized run-rate by the end of the first 30 months after closing, and approximately $500 million in annualized run-rate cost synergies within 18 to 24 months after closing, primarily from data centre infrastructure, vendors and operations.

What to watch next

Two gates remain before the deal can close: a vote by Zscaler shareholders and required regulatory approvals. The companies will file a registration statement on Form S-4 with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including a Zscaler proxy statement, according to the announcement. Until then, the $43.9 billion figure remains the value implied by CrowdStrike's November 20 share price — because Zscaler shareholders are being paid in CrowdStrike stock, the value they ultimately receive will move with that share price.
